visual_goal: Show the five ERP coexistence patterns as five lanes, ordered from most to least centralized, each with a differently labeled arrow showing what crosses it.
prompt: Five horizontal lanes stacked from top to bottom, each a thin soft-colored band with a short title at its left edge. A vertical gradient bar at the far right edge fades from dark blue at the top to pale at the bottom, showing centralization decreasing downward. Top lane, titled 'Single instance': a cluster of small office buildings with one thick arrow labeled 'transactions' into an open ledger book. Second lane, titled 'Two-tier': a small server box with one arrow labeled 'trial balance' into a larger server box with an open ledger book. Third lane, titled 'Central finance': a few small server boxes with one arrow labeled 'documents' into a funnel, then one arrow from the funnel into an open ledger book. Fourth lane, titled 'Accounting hub': a few small storefront platforms with one arrow labeled 'events' into a gear-shaped engine, then one arrow from the engine into an open ledger book. Bottom lane, titled 'Federation': several small independent server boxes, each with its own little book, with arrows labeled 'mapped balances' merging into one stacked-layers box labeled 'Consolidation'. Each lane flows left to right.
alt: Five lanes, from most to least centralized: single instance sending transactions, two-tier sending a trial balance, central finance sending documents through mapping, an accounting hub sending events through an engine, and a federation sending mapped balances to consolidation.

visual_goal: Show a tier-2 ERP whose every inbound and outbound flow is a contract: identities, chart and rates in from golden sources; intercompany across through an interface; trial balances and events out under control totals; consolidation locks only after certified reconciliations.
prompt: A left-to-right flow centered on one server box labeled 'Tier-2 ERP' in the middle. At the far left, two source boxes stacked: 'Entity register' with a small key icon on top and 'Rate service' with a small currency-exchange icon below; one arrow from each into 'Tier-2 ERP'. Above and to the right, a narrow gateway box 'Intercompany interface' receives one arrow from 'Tier-2 ERP' and sends one arrow into a larger server box 'Tier-1 core' at the upper right. To the right of 'Tier-2 ERP', a stacked-layers box 'Consolidation' receives one arrow from 'Tier-2 ERP' and one arrow down from 'Tier-1 core'. Below 'Tier-2 ERP', a horizontal pipe with lightning bolts labeled 'Event backbone' receives one arrow from 'Tier-2 ERP'. At the far right, a calendar with a padlock labeled 'Close lock' receives one arrow from 'Consolidation'. Every arrow carries a small signed paper contract tag with a tick mark, showing each flow has an owner and a proof. Exactly eight arrows.
alt: A tier-2 ERP receiving identities and rates from golden sources, sending intercompany entries through an interface to the tier-1 core, sending trial balances to consolidation and events to an event backbone, with every arrow tagged as a signed contract and the close locked after consolidation.

visual_goal: Show Northmere's 2030 finance estate: brand platforms feed one event backbone and one accounting engine into the S/4HANA group core; Tablekin on Workday is the only second ledger, joined by contract; OneStream consolidates two trial-balance sources.
prompt: A left-to-right architecture illustration on a light background. At the far left, three storefront boxes stacked: 'Stayloft', 'Wayfare', 'Ad billing', each with one short arrow into a horizontal pipe with lightning bolts labeled 'Event backbone'. Next, one arrow from the pipe into a large gear-shaped engine labeled 'Accounting engine', with a small rulebook beside it. Next, one arrow from the engine into a large open ledger book labeled 'S/4HANA core'. At the far right, a stacked-layers box labeled 'OneStream' with one arrow from 'S/4HANA core' into it. Directly below the engine, a small checklist box labeled 'BlackLine' with one short arrow straight down from the engine into it. Directly below 'S/4HANA core', a smaller separate ledger box labeled 'Tablekin'; one short arrow goes straight up from 'Tablekin' into 'S/4HANA core', and a small handshake icon sits on that arrow; one more arrow goes from 'Tablekin' to the right and up into 'OneStream'. Exactly eight arrows, none crossing another.
alt: Stayloft, Wayfare and ad billing feed an event backbone into one accounting engine that posts to the S/4HANA group core and sends breaks to BlackLine; Tablekin is a separate ledger joined to the core by agreement; OneStream consolidates two sources, the core and Tablekin.

visual_goal: Show an acquired ledger's path: deal close, day one, wrapping within 12 months, then one of three governed end states, with dated reviews on every state except convergence.
prompt: A board-game path of rounded stepping stones from left to right; each stone carries its own label written once, inside the stone. At the far left a handshake icon labeled 'Deal closes', then one single straight arrow to a stone 'Day one', then a stone 'Wrapping' with a small ribbon and a little clock labeled '12 months', then a larger stone 'Wrapped'. From 'Wrapped' the path forks into three branches fanning to the right: the top branch to a green stone 'Converge' with a finish flag; the middle branch to a blue stone 'Second tier'; the bottom branch to an orange stone 'Keep wrapped'. To the right of the middle and bottom stones sits one stone 'Review' with a calendar icon. One arrow from 'Keep wrapped' into 'Review'; a pair of arrows loops between 'Second tier' and 'Review' in both directions; one arrow curves from 'Review' up to 'Converge'.
alt: An acquired ledger moves from deal close through day one and wrapping within 12 months to wrapped, then to converge, second tier, or keep wrapped; the latter two go through a dated review that can lead back to second tier or on to converge.
